{{Short description|Canadian mathematician, playwright and author}}
'''John Mighton''', [[Order of Canada|O.C.]]  born in [[Hamilton, Ontario]], Canada on October 2, 1957, is a Canadian mathematician, playwright and best-selling author, who is known for his work to support children's successful math education.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About John Mighton - JUMP Math |url=https://jumpmath.org/ca/about/john-mighton/}}</ref> Mighton founded JUMP Math as a charity in 2002 and developed the JUMP Math program to address student underachievement in math. Mighton has won national and international awards for his contributions to both math education and Canadian theatre as an internationally recognized playwright.<ref name=cenc>{{Cite web |title=John Mighton - The Canadian Encyclopedia |url=https://www.thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/john-mighton}}</ref>

In 1997 Mighton played a mathematician in the film ''[[Good Will Hunting]]''.

== Education ==
Mighton earned a BA (Philosophy) at the University of Toronto (1978) and a MA (Philosophy) at McMaster University (1984).,<ref name=cenc/> later earning a PhD (Mathematics) at the [[University of Toronto]]. He was awarded an [[NSERC]] fellowship for his postdoctoral research in [[Knot theory|knot]] and [[graph theory]].<ref name=bio>{{Cite web |title=John Mighton Biography |url=https://jumpmath.org/ca/wp-content/uploads/sites/1/2022/09/John-Mighton-BiographySE2022.pdf}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences]] and has taught mathematics and math education at the University of Toronto. Mighton has also lectured in philosophy at [[McMaster University]].<ref name=bio/>

== Career ==
Mighton's plays have been performed in theatres worldwide and have been honoured with multiple awards, including the [[Siminovitch Prize in Theatre]], two Governor General’s Literary Awards for Drama, three Dora Awards, and the Chalmers Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dora Awards |url=https://tapa.ca/doras/recipients}}</ref> His plays include: ''Possible Worlds'', ''The Little Years'', ''Body & Soul'', ''Scientific Americans'', ''A Short History of Night'', and ''Half Life''.<ref name=bio/>

In 1997, Mighton was the math consultant and also played the role of “Tom”, an assistant to the math professor, in the critically acclaimed film, ''[[Good Will Hunting]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IMDB |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119217/?ref_=nm_ov_bio_lk}}</ref>

In 1998, Mighton started a small-scale tutoring group to assist children experiencing challenges in math, though he had abandoned the subject himself for years after struggling with math in school and nearly failing first-year calculus in university.

In 2002 Mighton founded JUMP (Junior Undiscovered Math Prodigies) Math, a Canadian charitable organization with the mission to enable every child to learn and love math.<ref>{{Cite web |title=JUMP Math Website |url=https://jumpmath.org/ca/about/}}</ref>

Mighton has written three books on math, based on his expertise and experiences with JUMP Math, including ''The Myth of Ability: Nurturing Mathematical Talent in Every Child (2003)'', which describes his approach and successes with JUMP Math; ''The End of Ignorance: Multiplying Our Human Potential (2007)'' as a further exploration of his philosophy and methods; and ''All Things Being Equal: Why Math is the Key to a Better World (2020)''.

* Margaret Sinclair Memorial Award for Innovation & Excellence, [[Fields Institute|The Fields Institute]] for Research in Mathematical Sciences (2022) <ref>{{Cite web |title=Fields Institute |url=http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/news/John-Mighton-JUMP-Math-founder-wins-2022-Margaret-Sinclair-Memorial-Award}}</ref>
* [[Adrien Pouliot Award]] for Outstanding Contributions to Math Education, [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] (2022) <ref>{{Cite web |title=Canadian Mathematical Society |url=https://cms.math.ca/news-item/mighton-2022-adrien-pouliot-award/#:~:text=John%20Mighton%20(JUMP%20Math)%20is,outstanding%20contributions%20to%20mathematics%20education}}</ref>
* President’s Award, [[Professional Engineers Ontario]] (2020) <ref>{{Cite web |title=Professional Engineers Ontario |url=https://www.peo.on.ca/about-peo/awards/presidents-award  }}</ref>
* [[World Innovation Summit for Education|WISE]] Award for Innovation in Education (2016) <ref>{{Cite web |title=Wise Qatar |url=https://www.wise-qatar.org/innovators-directory/project-type/126/}}</ref> 
* 10th Annual Egerton Ryerson Award for Dedication to Public Education (2016) <ref>{{Cite web |title=People for Education |url=http://www.peopleforeducation.ca/pfe-news/john-mighton-to-be-honoured/ |access-date=2017-06-26 |archive-date=2017-06-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170604202905/http://www.peopleforeducation.ca/pfe-news/john-mighton-to-be-honoured/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* [[Schwab Foundation for Social Entrepreneurship|Schwab Foundation]] Social Entrepreneur of the Year (2015) <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2015/03/meet-the-2015-social-entrepreneurs-of-the-year/|title=Meet the 2015 Social Entrepreneurs of the Year|website=World Economic Forum}}</ref>
* [[Ernst & Young Entrepreneur of the Year Award|Ernst & Young]] Social Entrepreneur of the Year (2014) <ref>{{Cite web |title=E&Y Newsroom |url=http://www.ey.com/ca/en/about-us/entrepreneurship/entrepreneur-of-the-year/ey-entrepreneur-of-the-year-national-2014-award-winners}}</ref>
* Officer of the [[Order of Canada]] (2010) <ref>{{Cite web |title=Order of Canada |url=https://www.gg.ca/en/honours/recipients/146-12240}}</ref>
* [[Ashoka: Innovators for the Public|Ashoka]] Fellow (2004) <ref>{{Cite web |title=Ashoka |url=https://www.ashoka.org/en-ca/fellow/john-mighton}}</ref>
